points: **Host factors:** HLA alleles (see *Stevens–Johnson syndrome / toxic epidermal necrolysis*), viral infection (EBV + amoxicillin; HIV ↑ sulfonamide reactions; HHV-6 reactivation in DRESS), older age, renal impairment, autoimmune disease.

items.name: Urticarial / angioedema
items.where: Penicillins/cephalosporins, NSAIDs/aspirin, opioids, contrast; ACE-i (angioedema, weeks–years)

items.name: Photosensitive (face, V of neck, backs of hands, sparing behind ears/under chin)
Blistering
items.where: SJS/TEN: allopurinol, carbamazepine, lamotrigine, phenytoin, sulfonamides, oxicam NSAIDs, nevirapine. FDE: NSAIDs, co-trimoxazole, tetracyclines, paracetamol. **DPP-4 inhibitors (gliptins) → bullous pemphigoid**. Naproxen → pseudoporphyria. Furosemide/ACE-i/PD-1 inhibitors → BP

items.name: Pustular (AGEP)
items.where: Aminopenicillins, macrolides, pristinamycin, hydroxychloroquine, diltiazem, terbinafine

items.name: Fever + rash + organ involvement (DRESS)
items.where: Allopurinol, carbamazepine, phenytoin, lamotrigine, sulfonamides, dapsone, minocycline, vancomycin

items.name: Lichenoid
items.where: Thiazides, β-blockers, ACE-i, antimalarials, gold, PD-1 inhibitors

points: a previous reaction to the same or a cross-reacting drug; re-exposure shortens the latency.
pattern (above), **mucosal involvement**, skin pain, Nikolsky sign, blisters/detachment (% BSA), pustules, facial oedema, lymphadenopathy, purpura.

**Naranjo** — a general ADR probability scale (10 questions; ≥9 definite, 5–8 probable, 1–4 possible, ≤0 doubtful); **ALDEN** — specific to SJS/TEN (see *Stevens–Johnson syndrome / toxic epidermal necrolysis*); **RegiSCAR** — DRESS scoring

items.t: Skin pain, blisters, skin detachment or mucosal erosions: possible **SJS/TEN**, stop the drug and admit the same day.
Fever, facial swelling, lymph nodes and abnormal bloods 2–8 weeks after a new drug: possible **DRESS**.
Swelling of lips, tongue or throat, or breathing difficulty: **999**.

pearls.t: "**Any rash on any drug** — take a dated drug history, then think SCAR red flags."

Give the patient the **drug name, the reaction and the date** in writing; advise wearing a medical alert if severe; check OTC products (ibuprofen) and combination products contain none of the culprit.
Write the reaction, not just "allergy", in the record (e.g. "amoxicillin — maculopapular rash day 7, 2026, no mucosal involvement").
